qs.q: An infant with sickle cell anaemia is brought to the clinic for routine preventative care. Which prophylactic intervention should be initiated from 2 months of age to prevent pneumococcal sepsis?
qs.e: Penicillin prophylaxis is recommended from 2 months of age until at least age 5 to prevent pneumococcal sepsis caused by functional asplenia. Hydroxyurea is not typically initiated at this very young age for uncomplicated primary prevention.
qs.s: Sickle Cell Disease: Pathology, Genetics & Mechanisms — Notes: MCQs

qs.q: A molecular analysis of a patient with sickle cell anaemia reveals a specific point mutation in the beta-globin chain. Which amino acid substitution characterizes this condition?
o: Valine for glutamic acid at position 6
Glutamic acid for valine at position 6
Lysine for glutamic acid at position 26
Alanine for valine at position 6 residue
qs.e: Sickle cell anaemia is caused by the substitution of valine for glutamic acid at the sixth position of the beta-globin chain. This single amino acid change promotes hemoglobin polymerization under low oxygen tension.
